SOURCES. (1) Agronomy Report 2/2026, visit 9 October 2026 by Senior Agronomist Mr. Lai Hong Heng (previous agronomy visit 17 April 2026); data as at September 2026; sets the 2027 fertiliser programme. (2) PA Report 1/2026, visit 29 June 2026 by Planting Advisor En. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff; reviews Jan-May 2026; still the latest PA report. (3) Earlier: Agronomy Report 1/2026 (17 April 2026, revised 2026 programme), PA 2/2025 (10 Dec 2025, Jan-Nov 2025), Agro 2/2025 (18 Nov 2025, original 2026 programme), PA 1/2025 and Agro 1/2025 (June 2025, 2025 programme). Agronomy reports call P13B "P12B"/"13B" and P13D "14D"/"P14D".

AREA (PA 1/2026, May 2026; Agro 2/2026 Tables 1-3). Total 1,416.43 ha; all 1,392.50 ha mature, buildings 23.93 ha. Fields (ha, PA SPH): P12A 2012 161.40 (133), P13B 2013 141.80 (133), P13C 2013 301.20 (133), P13D 2013 243.30 (136), P14E 2014 202.80 (121), P14F 2014 232.20 (136), P14G 2014 109.80 (136). Agro 2/2026 census: 189,376 palms, average 132 SPH (previous 136); P14E 120 SPH after elephant damage (census Sep 2025); other blocks last censused 2022 per Agro 2/2026 (Agro 1/2026 said Feb 2024); census now under way in P13D. Palms prime, 12-14 years. Agro: 432.2 ha (31%) low-lying flood-prone and 165 ha (11.8%) peat (all peat in P13C: C1 20, C2 40, C3 30, C4 15, C5 30, C6 30 ha). PA: topography flat, cambered bunds over 900 ha.

YIELD (Agro 2/2026 section 5). Estate t/ha by year: 2019 15.87, 2020 18.80, 2021 19.64 (peak), 2022 19.49, 2023 17.87, 2024 18.67, 2025 18.29 (6.9% below the 2021 peak). Jan-Sep 2026 vs Jan-Sep 2025 (Table 17, t/ha): P12A 16.82 vs 13.35 (+26%); P13B 17.8 vs 14.93 (+19%); P13C 13.71 vs 11.83 (+16%); P13D 14.67 vs 13.86 (+6%); P14E 10.39 vs 10.21 (+1%); P14F 16.72 vs 15.81 (+6%); P14G 9.59 vs 7.87 (+22%); estate 14.34 vs 12.79 (+12%). Still below potential for prime palms. P14E only slightly up because of 120 SPH, foliage damage and toppling by elephants. P14G lowest because of tapping-rights issues in P14G1 and P14G2 (2025 10.48 t/ha vs 16.50 in 2024, -36.5%). Agro 2/2026 prints no FFB tonnages. Main limiting factor: prolonged high water table and flooding in low-lying areas, with 4,821 mm rain a year and 33.5 mm per rain day. Table 18 (period not stated): higher ground 480.7 ha 17.4 t/ha, bunch 14.61 kg; flooded 911.8 ha 12.54 t/ha, 12.69 kg (-28% yield, -13% bunch weight). By block (higher vs flooded t/ha): P12A 17.44 vs 16.27 (-7%); P12B 18.28 vs 17.41 (-5%); P13C 17.93 vs 11.11 (-38%); P13D 18.49 vs 10.92 (-41%); P14E 13.93 vs 7.53 (-46%); P14F 18.34 vs 14.96 (-18%); P14G all flooded 109.8 ha 9.59.

PRODUCTION (PA 1/2026). Jan-May 2026: 9,116.16 t FFB vs budget 9,300.00 t and 8,932.09 t same period 2025; 6.55 t/ha vs budget 6.68 and 6.41 last year; annual budget 30,000 t (21.54 t/ha). HARVESTING. Agro 2/2026: intervals Jan-Sep 2026 ranged 13-20 days, averaging 15-17 days (target 15); overripe 4-7% in freshly harvested bunches (P13D5 6%, P12B1 7%, P14F1 4%, P13C4 7%), the main field loss; leftover rotten bunches increased though occasional (P13D3, P12B1, P12A3, P12A1); incomplete loose fruit collection minimal; overall acceptable. LEAF (Agro 2/2026 Appendix 2, 28 samples received 31/1/2026). N moderately low to low in 71% of samples and Mg in 75%; K, B and Ca mostly normal; P generally adequate. FERTILISER PROGRAMME 2027 (Agro 2/2026 Appendix 1, kg/palm; shown in grams on the Blocks tab). P12A: Mix B 2.50 Feb, RP 1.50 Mar, Mix B 2.00 May, Mix B 2.25 (A1) or 2.50 (A2, A3) Jul, Mix B 2.00 Oct. P13B: NK2 2.50 Feb, RP 1.50 Mar, Mix B 2.00 May, kieserite 0.50 (B1, B2) or 0.75 (B3) Jun, NK2 2.25 (B1, B2) or 2.50 (B3) Jul, Mix B 2.00 Oct. P13C: NK2 2.25 Feb, RP 1.75 (C1-C3) or 1.50 (C4-C6) Mar, NK2 2.25 (C1-C3) or 2.00 (C4-C6) May, kieserite 0.50 Jun, Mix B 2.00 Jul and Oct. P13D: D1, D2, D5 NK2 2.25 Feb and May, RP 1.50 (1.75 D2) Mar, kieserite 0.50 Jun (D1, D5), Mix B 2.00 Jul and Oct; D3, D4 RP 1.50 Mar plus Mix B 8.0* Apr. P14E: E1 Mix B 2.25 Feb, RP 1.50 Mar, Mix B 2.00 May, kieserite 0.75 Jun, Mix B 2.00 Jul and Oct; E2-E4 RP 1.50-1.75 Mar plus Mix B 8.0* Apr. P14F: F1-F4 NK3 2.25-2.50 Feb, RP 1.50-1.75 Mar, NK3 2.25 May, 0.50 Jun (fertiliser not named), Mix B 2.00 Jul and Oct; F5 RP 1.50 plus Mix B 8.0* Apr. P14G (appendix titled 2026): RP 1.50 Mar plus Mix B 8.0* (G3 Apr, G1 and G2 May). 8.0* doses are sub-soil applications. NK2 = 60% SOA, 40% MOP; NK3 = 40% SOA, 60% MOP; Mix B = 45% AS, 40% MOP, 14% KIE, 1% borate. New planting or supply: 600 g controlled-release fertiliser (20:6:14:3) and 500 g RP in the planting hole, then nothing for 9 months. Compared with 2026, the 2027 programme drops GML, brings back kieserite in June, uses NK3 in P14F and raises the July/October Mix B doses (2026 revised programme had Mix B 1.25-1.50 kg in Jul and Oct). 2026 revised programme (Agro 1/2026): Feb NK2 or Mix B 2.00-2.50 kg, Mar RP 1.50-1.75, May NK2 or Mix B 2.00, Jun GML 1.50, Jul and Oct Mix B 1.25-1.50, with 8 kg Mix B sub-soil in flood/peat sub-blocks. 2025 programme (Agro 1/2025): Mix B 2.00-2.25 kg in Feb, May, Jul and Oct, RP 1.50-2.00 Mar, kieserite 1.00 Jun in some sub-blocks.

Weed control improved since April: higher ground mostly acceptable, low ground from largely unacceptable to moderately acceptable-acceptable; wild pandan much reduced along drains (P13D3, P13D5); bare ground much reduced (slightly bare P13D1, P14E1); strip and blanket spraying greatly reduced but path spraying seen in P13D2; incomplete weed kill occasional (P13C5); Clidemia flowering in P14E1. Peat (P13C5) still bare or under Stenochlaena and Dicranopteris ferns: keep Nephrolepis in the inter-row and establish Lindernia on paths (as at Juasa B). Use one-sided or baffle-screen covers. PA 1/2026 (Jan-May 2026): circle spraying 1,554.90 ha vs 1,392.50 due; selective 2,311.50 of 2,785.00 ha (83%).

PRUNING. Agro 2/2026 Table 9 (Sep 2026): round 1 1,392.50 ha (100%); round 2 564 ha (41%), balance 828.5 ha (P12A 50%, P13B 60%, P13C 30%, P13D 39%, P14E 32%, P14F 43%, P14G 46%). Quality acceptable; high/low ground gap much reduced; hanging fronds on some palms; many palms slightly over-pruned (P12B2). Elephant-damaged palms (P13D3, P13D5, P14E1, P14G3): prune only dry hanging fronds. PA 1/2026: progressive pruning 100% Jan-May 2026.

PESTS. Rats (Agro 2/2026 Table 14): first baiting Jan 2026 (P13D, P14E, P14F, P14G) or Feb 2026 (P12A, P13B, P13C), then censuses; second baiting Aug 2026 in P12A1 (15%), P13C1 (15%), P13C6 (17%), P13D4 (16%), P14E2 (16%) and Sep 2026 in P14F5 (12%), P14G3 (18%); other sub-blocks 5-9%. Estate followed the advice. Next: post-baiting census; round 1 one bait per palm, census after one month, round 2 with bait replaced every 7 days until consumption is below 20%; bait must stay palatable 7 days; opened bait used the same day. Barn owls (Table 15): 103 of 105 boxes, 89 occupied this month vs 93 last month (86%); text says up to 86% from 56%; cleaning 42 to date; repair or replace damaged boxes. PA May 2026: 92 occupied (89%). Elephants: damage worse since Nov 2025, numerous palms toppled; fences at P14E1/P14E4 (Hutan Simpan Lesong) and P13C5/P13C6 (Hutan Simpan Berabong); vegetation touching cables (P14E1), gaps between lowest cable and drains, extra low cables may touch floodwater. PA: 15 palms toppled in P13D and P14E; 4 km fencing with Sawak and Delima. Bagworm: none in 2026 (PA); 1,870 chains of predator plants.

DRAINAGE AND FIELD. Agro 2/2026: 2-ft drains on both sides of cambered bunds in low-lying P12A, P13D, P14E, P14F, P14G, soil used for mounding; Table 11 Jun-Sep 2026: P12A 137.88, P13D 410.06, P14E 62.18, P14F 418.80, P14G 278.07, total 1,306.99. Palm vigour improved where drained; stunted palms remain in low-lying patches (P14D5, P14E1). Keep main drains free-flowing; blocked drains in P14E2; culverts above drain water level in P13C1. Flood-prone sub-blocks (Table 10, flooded ha): A3 20.0, B3 20.0, C1 40.0, D3 40.0, D4 40.0, D5 30.0, E1 20.0, E2 30.9, E3 30.9, E4 40.4, F4 30.0, F5 35.0, G2 20.0, G3 35.0 = 432.2 of 665.6 ha. RAINFALL (mm, days): 2021 4,512.5/154; 2022 5,040.5/178; 2023 6,278.5/157; 2024 4,136.5/108; 2025 4,139.5/125 (PA); Jan-May 2026 809.5/27. Agro 2/2026 Table 5 (2021-2025): 2025 4,138 mm, 5-year average 4,821 mm.

KEY ACTIONS. Better harvesting supervision (overripe, rotten bunches); post-baiting rat census and follow-up baiting; elephant fence fixes; finish the palm census; recommended frond stacking; targeted weeding and peat ground cover; continue drainage schedule and clear culverts; EFB at 50 t/ha on high ground; resume thinning; remove hanging fronds, avoid over-pruning; barn owl box repair and cleaning; follow the 2027 programme; recruit harvesters; P14G security (PA).
